incidents.vector: A GitHub employee installed a poisoned version of the Nx Console VS Code extension, which had been republished to the Marketplace using stolen maintainer credentials.
incidents.impact: Roughly 3,800 GitHub-internal repositories were exfiltrated and offered for sale for $50,000 on a cybercrime forum. GitHub says customer data and repositories were not affected; critical secrets were rotated and the device isolated.

incidents.victim: Mini Shai-Hulud npm/PyPI supply-chain wave (@antv, TanStack, Mistral AI, UiPath, OpenSearch and others)
incidents.vector: A self-replicating worm published via compromised maintainer accounts and a no-credential CI exploit chain (Pwn Request, GitHub Actions cache poisoning, OIDC token theft from runner memory) executed during npm install to steal GitHub, AWS, npm, Vault, Kubernetes and 1Password credentials.
incidents.impact: GitHub removed 640 malicious packages and invalidated 61,274 npm tokens; hundreds of packages across @antv, @tanstack, @mistralai, @uipath, OpenSearch and others were poisoned (one wave: 373 malicious versions across 169 packages). OpenAI confirmed two engineers were compromised and rotated code-signing certificates.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters compromised a Salesforce instance used by 7-Eleven to store franchisee documents.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses and Social Security numbers of franchisees were stolen; 7-Eleven filed breach notifications in Maine, Vermont and Massachusetts. Discovered April 8, disclosed May 19-20.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion attributed to the Nitrogen gang disrupted Foxconn's North American manufacturing operations.
incidents.impact: Foxconn confirmed the incident after workers leaked internal messages; Nitrogen claims it stole 8TB of data including confidential chip designs and project documents for Apple, Google and NVIDIA orders.

incidents.victim: Central Asian and Middle East telecoms (Afghanistan ISP, Azerbaijan, others)
incidents.vector: Chinese espionage clusters, including the group tracked as Calypso / Red Lamassu, deployed a previously undocumented Linux backdoor called Showboat (aka kworker) alongside a Windows backdoor.
incidents.impact: Multi-year intrusions at telecoms and ISPs in Afghanistan, Azerbaijan and other small markets enabled traffic interception and lateral movement to non-internet-connected LAN devices, with zero VirusTotal detections at the time of discovery.

incidents.victim: US gas station fuel tank gauges
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited internet-exposed automatic tank gauge (ATG) systems that lacked password protection at US gas stations.
incidents.impact: Display readings on fuel tanks were altered, though actual fuel levels and physical safety systems were not affected. The attack coincides with the active US-Israel-Iran conflict and is read as strategic signalling against US critical infrastructure.

incidents.vector: A Nightwing contractor working for CISA disabled GitHub secret-scanning and used a public 'Private-CISA' repo as a personal scratchpad, exposing AWS GovCloud admin keys, internal artifactory credentials, and plaintext passwords for dozens of internal CISA systems.
incidents.impact: Three highly privileged AWS GovCloud accounts and CISA's internal DevSecOps and artifactory systems were exposed for roughly six months. Keys remained valid for 48 hours after the repo was taken offline. Sen. Maggie Hassan demanded a classified briefing by June 5; CISA says no sensitive data was confirmed compromised.

incidents.vector: Attackers likely exploited a cryptography flaw in THORChain's threshold ECDSA implementation, accumulating leaked key material over months to reconstruct a wallet private key.
incidents.impact: $10.7 million in crypto assets were drained; THORChain suspended trading.

incidents.vector: A group calling itself the CoinbaseCartel breached Grafana and exfiltrated GitHub repositories before issuing a ransom demand.
incidents.impact: Grafana refused to pay, citing recent FBI guidance against paying extortionists. The repository data is at risk of public release.

incidents.vector: Hotel check-in platform Tabiq left an AWS storage bucket accessible without authentication.
incidents.impact: More than one million passports and other government-issued ID documents from hotel guests were exposed online.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to systems containing patient medical and biometric records.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people had medical data and biometric information including fingerprints and palm prints stolen — irreplaceable identifiers compromised for life.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached RXNT, an electronic prescription platform, in March 2026.
incidents.impact: Patient prescription data was stolen, including records of members of the US Congress who use RXNT for prescriptions. The company notified regulators on the final day allowed under US health privacy laws.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited a flaw in Instructure's Free-for-Teacher accounts to gain repeated access to the Canvas platform across at least three separate intrusions since September 2025.
incidents.impact: Names, email addresses, student IDs and inter-user messages for users at thousands of schools were stolen; the Canvas login page was defaced with a ransom demand during finals week, disrupting roughly 9,000 universities and K-12 districts. Instructure paid the ransom and ShinyHunters claims it destroyed the data; the FBI urged victims not to pay.

incidents.vector: Attackers published hundreds of malicious Ruby packages targeting RubyGems staff with cross-site scripting and data theft payloads.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new user sign-ups while investigating; details of what data was stolen from staff remain unclear. Unrelated to the parallel TanStack/npm supply chain wave.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack on West Pharmaceutical, a major manufacturer of pharmaceutical drug packaging and delivery components.
incidents.impact: Global business operations including manufacturing, shipping and receiving were disrupted, per an SEC filing. Some sites have since restored operations.

incidents.vector: The Lapsus$ group leaked source code stolen from Vodafone after the EU telco refused to pay an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: Internal source code was published online; downstream security and competitive implications still being assessed.

incidents.vector: Attackers maintained undetected access to Best Western's reservation systems from October 2025 through April 2026.
incidents.impact: Guest reservation data across Best Western, Sure Hotels and WorldHotels brands was likely accessed during a six-month dwell time. The company is notifying affected guests.

incidents.vector: Maliciously crafted network traffic exploited a previously undisclosed zero-day in Huawei VRP enterprise router software, sending devices into a continuous restart loop.
incidents.impact: Mobile, landline and emergency communications across Luxembourg went down for over three hours on July 23, 2025; the vulnerability still has no CVE 10 months later and Huawei has issued no public advisory. Newly reported May 19, 2026.
